entries.title: The Chat guide answers questions about the piece
entries.body: The guide in the Chat panel answers a question about a passage, term or claim in at most three short sentences, pointing to the passages behind its answer, where before it declined, then offers to carry on in Chat in your own words. It suggests where to start before asking anything, no longer asks about you or quotes your profile back, and does not assume you have read the piece unless you say so. Talking to the article out loud, the guide also suggests first and leaves personal questions alone.

entries.title: Adding an article shows its progress more clearly
entries.body: While a PDF is added, a progress bar counts the sections read and images collected. When the article is ready, a green tick says so at the top, with Open the article at both ends of the page. The box for why you are reading sits near the top, and an empty profile gets a box about you too.

entries.title: Every conversation follows the same principles
entries.body: The AI in Chat, Learn, the guide and other conversations shares one set of instructions: leave you sharper, and get you there sooner than you would alone; be candid rather than agreeable; when you push back, recheck, then hold or revise the answer and say why; say how it knows each thing; and point you to other parts of Spideryarn.

entries.title: Citations in the margin show the full card
entries.body: In the notes in the margin beside the article, pointing at a Cites line opens the same card a citation in the text shows, with the same buttons, such as asking about it or opening it in Sources. Any other margin line that is cut short shows its full words when you point at it.

entries.title: The position strip explains its colours
entries.body: The card for a section of the strip showing where you are in the article explains what the strip is, with a key to the colours and marks drawn on it, in windows tall enough to fit it. In Ideas, Timeline and Referee, the card counts that mode's passages rather than calling them search matches.

entries.title: Feedback's Send and Cancel are green and red
entries.body: In the Feedback dialog, the buttons that send are green and the ones that leave without sending, such as Cancel and Close, are red, so they are easier to tell apart. Red does not mean anything is deleted: Cancel keeps your draft.

entries.title: A failed import shows why, and offers Retry
entries.body: Opening your own article after its import had failed told you the article was not shared. It shows why the import failed and a Retry button instead, and follows the newest attempt once you retry.

entries.title: Tables in PDFs keep their columns
entries.body: Some tables in PDFs were drawn with each row run together into one cell, or with the headings a column out. Tables are read cell by cell, so rows and columns line up. This applies to PDFs added from here on; ones already in your library are not redone automatically.
